enumeration_note: One taught skeleton â€” fade/reversal scalp at HTF-marked liquidity zones after a sweep+rejection on the 5m/1m, stop beyond the swept level, 1:2 target. Long-at-support and short-at-resistance are the symmetric two sides of the same mean-reversion setup (not opposition). Timeframe (5m/1m), single-tap vs double-rejection confirmation, and session are compatible variants grouped under one strategy.

coaching_notes: Market makers push price into liquidity to fill large orders â€” anticipate where price is going, not react to it
Find where the obvious trades are sitting and do the opposite
Look for clean price action that's just a little too clean â€” equal highs, trend lines, or zones that look perfect; that's the bait
Avoid entering before the price taps the liquidity zone. Wait for confirmation.
Do not chase the breakouts. Wait for price to trap traders and fade the move.
element_inventory: PRECONDITION: mark higher-time-frame (daily/4h) most recent swing highs/lows and clean untapped support/resistance levels first before dropping down
PRECONDITION: identify HTF zones that have not been tapped yet (where liquidity is living)
ENTRY: on 5m/1m, wait for price to rapidly approach a marked zone with a volume spike, quick tap, and rejection
ENTRY CONFIRMATION: exhaustion candle, long wick, bullish/bearish engulfing candle, or volume divergence
TRAP CONFIRMATION: price wicks above resistance then dumps, or wicks below support then reverses
OCCURRENCE-SELECTION: only enter AFTER the liquidity zone is tapped â€” never before
DOUBLE-REJECTION VARIANT: two rejections of the same area with the bar not closing beyond the level (double bottom)
STOP: place stop below the swept level (e.g. below the current London low for a long at support)
TIMEFRAME: 5-minute (or 1-minute for riskier entries) execution; daily/4h for zone marking
SESSION FILTER: prefer London or New York open (when the most stop hunts happen)
FILTER: do not chase breakouts â€” fade the move after traders are trapped
strategies.entry_summary: Mark higher-time-frame (daily/4h) clean untapped support/resistance and swing highs/lows first. Drop to the 5-minute (or 1-minute) chart and wait for price to rapidly approach one of those marked zones with a volume spike, a quick tap, and a rejection wick. Enter the fade (reversal) on confirmation â€” an exhaustion candle, long wick, bullish/bearish engulfing, or volume divergence â€” only AFTER the zone is tapped. Traps confirm: price wicks above resistance then dumps, or wicks below support then reverses.
strategies.exit_summary: Stop loss below the level that was swept (e.g. below the current London low for a long at support); target a fixed 1:2 risk-to-reward. If price rejects the same area twice without the bar closing beyond the level (double bottom), take the reversal for another 1:2.
